title: CONGENITAL MYOPATHY 10B, MILD VARIANT
alt_titles: MYOPATHY, AREFLEXIA, RESPIRATORY DISTRESS, AND DYSPHAGIA, EARLY-ONSET, MILD VARIANT

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that the mild variant of congenital myopathy-10 (CMYO10B) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEGF10 gene (612453) on chromosome 5q23.

checks.claim: The mild variant of congenital myopathy-10 (CMYO10B) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEGF10 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: patients displaying a less severe phenotype, with later respiratory failure and minicores on muscle biopsy (mvEMARDD or with minicore myopathy), harbour homozygous or compound heterozygous missense variants affecting the cysteine in the EGF-like domain.
checks.explanation: The paper says the mild variant (mvEMARDD) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous MEGF10 variants.

checks.claim: The MEGF10 gene is located on chromosome 5q23.
checks.evidence_quote: MEGF10 lies within a linkage peak on chromosome 5 that reached the maximum possible LOD score of 1.329.
checks.explanation: Paper places MEGF10 on chromosome 5; band 5q23 is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Congenital myopathy-10B (CMYO10B) is an autosomal recessive muscle disorder that is a milder form of the myopathy caused by MEGF10 mutations. Patients have onset of proximal muscle weakness in childhood, often with mildly delayed motor milestones, and the disorder is slowly progressive. Features include respiratory insufficiency, which may appear in adulthood, scoliosis, and joint contractures or hyperlaxity. Muscle biopsy may show myopathic changes with minicores. The severe end of the spectrum, also called early-onset myopathy, areflexia, respiratory distress, and dysphagia (EMARDD), is called CMYO10A.

checks.claim: Congenital myopathy-10B (CMYO10B) is an autosomal recessive muscle disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: three of four siblings were affected with an unclassified autosomal recessive myopathy
checks.explanation: Autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: CMYO10B is a milder form of the myopathy caused by MEGF10 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotypes described therein are generally similar to those of families 1030 and 105, but are more severe.
checks.explanation: The paper describes its patients' phenotype as milder than the previously reported MEGF10 myopathy.

checks.claim: Patients with CMYO10B have onset of proximal muscle weakness in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected members of family 1030 presented with weakness by 12 months of age, initially in the neck. Weakness was present throughout the body but was primarily axial and proximal
checks.explanation: Weakness was primarily proximal and axial, but onset was in infancy (by 12 months; several weeks in 105-1), not specified as childhood.

checks.claim: Patients with CMYO10B often have mildly delayed motor milestones.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The paper reports no patients or clinical features.

checks.claim: CMYO10B is slowly progressive.
checks.evidence_quote: a 66 year old male with a 20 year history of progressive proximal and distal weakness of upper and lower limbs
checks.explanation: The abstract shows progression over 20 years in one patient, but it does not describe the disorder in general as slowly progressive.

checks.claim: Features of CMYO10B include respiratory insufficiency, which may appear in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas with 2 missense mutations, respiratory dysfunction occurs at 10 years old or much later, as in the patient reported here
checks.explanation: The patient developed respiratory failure in his 50s, which fits respiratory insufficiency starting in adulthood.

checks.claim: Features of CMYO10B include scoliosis.
checks.evidence_quote: All three patients had childhood onset scoliosis and were treated with spinal fusion surgery
checks.explanation: Scoliosis reported.

checks.claim: Features of CMYO10B include joint contractures or joint hyperlaxity.
checks.evidence_quote: Contractures of the neck were observed in infancy, and contractures of the elbows, knees, and heel cords developed by adulthood.
checks.explanation: Contractures in family 1030; hyperflexible joints in subject 105-1.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsy in CMYO10B may show myopathic changes with minicores.
checks.evidence_quote: However, moth-eaten fibers and minicores were also observed, suggestive of a congenital myopathy.
checks.explanation: Minicores on biopsy.

checks.claim: The severe end of the MEGF10-related myopathy spectrum, also called early-onset myopathy, areflexia, respiratory distress, and dysphagia (EMARDD), is called CMYO10A.
checks.evidence_quote: early-onset myopathy characterized by areflexia, respiratory distress, and dysphagia (EMARDD: OMIM 614399), and a milder phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract presents EMARDD as the more severe phenotype, but it does not use the name CMYO10A.

paragraphs.text: MEGF10-related myopathy forms a spectrum. The severe infantile form, EMARDD, is called CMYO10A. The milder form, which begins in childhood or later and may show minicores on biopsy, is called CMYO10B.

checks.claim: MEGF10-related myopathy forms a spectrum.
checks.evidence_quote: discuss the spectrum of MEGF10 related disease
checks.explanation: The abstract explicitly refers to a spectrum of MEGF10-related disease.

checks.claim: The severe infantile form of MEGF10-related myopathy, EMARDD, is called CMYO10A.
checks.evidence_quote: are known to cause early-onset myopathy characterized by areflexia, respiratory distress, and dysphagia (EMARDD: OMIM 614399)
checks.explanation: The abstract describes EMARDD as early-onset, but it does not use the CMYO10A name and does not say 'infantile'.

checks.claim: The milder form of MEGF10-related myopathy, which begins in childhood or later and may show minicores on biopsy, is called CMYO10B.
checks.evidence_quote: and a milder phenotype of minicore myopathy
checks.explanation: The abstract supports a milder minicore form, but it does not state onset in childhood or later and does not use the CMYO10B name.

paragraphs.text: Boyden et al. (2012) reported patients with a recessive congenital myopathy and MEGF10 mutations. Their phenotype was milder than the severe EMARDD phenotype. They had childhood-onset weakness, respiratory impairment, and scoliosis, and muscle biopsy showed minicores.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) reported patients with a recessive congenital myopathy and MEGF10 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the satellite cell gene MEGF10 cause a recessive congenital myopathy with minicores.
checks.explanation: Title states it.

checks.claim: The phenotype of the MEGF10 myopathy patients reported by Boyden et al. (2012) was milder than the severe EMARDD phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Nonsense and frameshift mutations in MEGF10 were recently determined to be the cause of a severe congenital myopathy with diaphragmatic weakness, areflexia, and dysphagia. ... The phenotypes described therein are generally similar to those of families 1030 and 105, but are more severe.
checks.explanation: Milder than the severe phenotype.

checks.claim: The MEGF10 myopathy patients reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had childhood-onset weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: Three siblings from a non-consanguineous nuclear family (1030) presented with childhood weakness, respiratory problems, and scoliosis.
checks.explanation: Childhood weakness.

checks.claim: The MEGF10 myopathy patients reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had respiratory impairment.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by severe weakness, respiratory impairment, scoliosis, joint contractures
checks.explanation: Respiratory impairment.

checks.claim: The MEGF10 myopathy patients reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had scoliosis.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by severe weakness, respiratory impairment, scoliosis, joint contractures
checks.explanation: Scoliosis.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsy in the MEGF10 myopathy patients reported by Boyden et al. (2012) showed minicores.
checks.evidence_quote: minicores were not noted in the biopsies from the reported families with null mutations but were a prominent feature in our patients with missense mutations.
checks.explanation: Minicores on biopsy.

paragraphs.text: Liewluck et al. (2016) reported patients with multiminicore myopathy caused by MEGF10 mutations. They had respiratory insufficiency beginning in adulthood, scoliosis, and hyperlaxity of the distal joints.

checks.claim: Liewluck et al. (2016) reported patients with multiminicore myopathy caused by MEGF10 mutations.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. This is Holterman et al. (2007), a mouse satellite cell study. It contains nothing about Liewluck et al. (2016) or multiminicore myopathy.

checks.claim: The multiminicore myopathy patients with MEGF10 mutations reported by Liewluck et al. (2016) had respiratory insufficiency beginning in adulthood.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The paper does not address patients or respiratory insufficiency.

checks.claim: The multiminicore myopathy patients with MEGF10 mutations reported by Liewluck et al. (2016) had scoliosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The paper does not address patients or scoliosis.

checks.claim: The multiminicore myopathy patients with MEGF10 mutations reported by Liewluck et al. (2016) had hyperlaxity of the distal joints.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The paper does not address patients or joint hyperlaxity.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of CMYO10B in the reported families was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance (Boyden et al., 2012).

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of CMYO10B in the families reported by Boyden et al. (2012) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We ascertained a non-consanguineous Caucasian family of mixed European ancestry in which three of four siblings had an undiagnosed autosomal recessive myopathy
checks.explanation: Autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: In patients with a mild congenital myopathy with minicores, Boyden et al. (2012) found homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the MEGF10 gene. They suggested that the mild phenotype was associated with missense mutations, whereas the severe EMARDD phenotype was associated with mutations that cause loss of function.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) found homozygous or compound heterozygous MEGF10 mutations in patients with a mild congenital myopathy with minicores.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected subjects were compound heterozygous for missense mutations c.976T > C (p.C326R) and c.2320T > C (p.C774R).
checks.explanation: Compound heterozygous mutations in family 1030 and only a single heterozygous mutation in 105-1; no homozygous mutations were found.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) suggested that the mild MEGF10-related myopathy phenotype was associated with missense mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: This difference is consistent with the total loss of detectable MEGF10 expression observed in the reported families, compared to the expected misfolding of MEGF10 protein due to disruption of disulfide bonds in family 1030.
checks.explanation: The authors link the milder phenotype to missense mutations.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) suggested that the severe EMARDD phenotype was associated with MEGF10 mutations that cause loss of function.
checks.evidence_quote: This difference is consistent with the total loss of detectable MEGF10 expression observed in the reported families
checks.explanation: The severe phenotype is linked to nonsense/frameshift mutations and loss of expression.

paragraphs.text: Liewluck et al. (2016) found novel MEGF10 mutations in adult patients with multiminicore disease.

checks.claim: Liewluck et al. (2016) found novel MEGF10 mutations in adult patients with multiminicore disease.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The paper reports no MEGF10 mutations in patients and does not refer to Liewluck et al. (2016).

paragraphs.text: Boyden et al. (2012) noted that patients with the milder myopathy carried at least one missense mutation in MEGF10. In contrast, patients with severe EMARDD (CMYO10A) usually had biallelic mutations that were predicted to cause loss of function.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) noted that patients with the milder MEGF10-related myopathy carried at least one missense mutation in MEGF10.
checks.evidence_quote: minicores were not noted in the biopsies from the reported families with null mutations but were a prominent feature in our patients with missense mutations.
checks.explanation: All of their milder patients carried missense mutations.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) noted that patients with severe EMARDD (CMYO10A) usually had biallelic MEGF10 mutations predicted to cause loss of function.
checks.evidence_quote: Nonsense and frameshift mutations in MEGF10 were recently determined to be the cause of a severe congenital myopathy with diaphragmatic weakness, areflexia, and dysphagia. One reported family was compound heterozygous for the c.2320T > C (p.C774R) missense mutation we identified in family 1030 and a frameshift mutation.
checks.explanation: Severe cases were mostly null mutations, with one missense/frameshift family, which fits 'usually'.
